To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a service model for wireless communication that has a number of desirable characteristics, and we present a wireless fair service algorithm that achieves this model in typical wireless environments.
we present an efficient algorithm for fair service over error‐prone channels, and that it is suitable for wireless networks.
we have defined and analyzed an algorithm for fair and bounded service in wireless channels, and that we have implemented it in a real wireless environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, analysis and implementation of a service model and an associated algorithm for fair service of real‐time and best effort data flows over a shared wireless medium with location‐dependent errors.
the design of an efficient, fair, and robust scheduling scheme for wireless communication networks.

the design of a wireless channel service model that supports diverse real‐time and error sensitive data applications, the design of a service algorithm that implements the service model, and the analysis of the service algorithm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents the design, analysis and implementation of an effective service model for fair service in wireless channels.

the algorithm provides the following benefits: it is simple, efficient, and robust, it is easy to implement and deploy, and it provides a high degree of service fairness and performance guarantees for a variety of data traffic flows in error‐proned wireless networks.
the algorithm provides a practical solution for providing fair service to real‐time and error‐prone traffic flows over wireless channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed and analyzed an algorithm for fair wireless service in error‐corrupted environments, and have shown that it achieves the service model requirements.
we present the first algorithm that supports fair service for real‐time and error sensitive flows in a wireless channel with bursty and location dependent errors.
we have designed and analyzed an algorithm that supports fair service in wireless channels with bounded channel errors, and that we have implemented this algorithm within the CSMA/CA framework.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to support a broad class of real‐time and error‐prone data flows over wireless channels with a service model that is both fair and predictable.

it is possible to achieve fairness in error‐prune wireless environments, even in the presence of bursty errors, and this is achieved by decoupling of service delay and bandwidth, and by graceful service compensation for flows that lag behind.
it is possible to design a service model that is fair to all data flows, and that can be implemented within the framework of existing MAC protocols.
